When `Faker` is constructed with a dict, `__init__` normalizes the locale keys into an `OrderedDict`, stores `locales = list(odict.keys())`, and stores `self._weights = list(odict.values())`. For `{"en_US": 1, "de_DE": 4, "ja_JP": 9}`, that makes `self._weights` equal to `[1, 4, 9]` in insertion order.

Later, `fake.word()` goes through `__getattr__` to `_select_factory("word")`, which calls `_map_provider_method`. Because `self._weights` is truthy, `_map_provider_method` zips `self.factories` with `self._weights`, keeps the pairs whose factory has `word`, then returns `list(factories), list(weights)`. The three locale-specific Faker factories support `word`, so the returned `weights` list is the same ordered list `[1, 4, 9]`. That is the object whose truthiness is tested by `if weights:`.
